questions.stem: In a metre bridge experiment, the balance point is 40 cm from the end of the wire next to the unknown resistor X. If the known resistor in the other gap is 6 ohms, find X.
questions.explanation: X/6 = 40/60, so X = 4 ohms.

questions.stem: A standard cell of e.m.f. 1.08 V balances at 54.0 cm on a potentiometer wire. Another cell balances at 75.0 cm. Find the e.m.f. of the second cell.
Resistors of 2 ohms, 3 ohms and 6 ohms are connected in parallel across a 12 V supply of negligible internal resistance. Find the total current drawn.
questions.explanation: The equivalent resistance is 1/(1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6) = 1 ohm, so I = 12/1 = 12 A.

questions.stem: Ohm's law states that, at constant temperature, the current through a metallic conductor is
options: inversely proportional to the potential difference
proportional to the square of the potential difference
directly proportional to the potential difference across it
questions.explanation: V = IR with R constant.

questions.stem: Resistors of 4 ohms and 8 ohms are connected in series across a 12 V supply. Find the p.d. across the 8 ohm resistor.
questions.explanation: The current is 12/12 = 1 A, so the p.d. across 8 ohms is 8 V.

questions.stem: The resistance of a metallic conductor increases when its temperature rises because
options: the vibrating ions obstruct the flow of electrons more
the number of free electrons falls to zero
the charge on each electron increases
questions.explanation: Greater lattice vibrations scatter the drift electrons more often.

questions.stem: A current of 3 A divides between a 3 ohm resistor and a 6 ohm resistor connected in parallel. Find the current in the 3 ohm resistor.
questions.explanation: The current divides inversely as the resistances, 2 : 1, so the 3 ohm resistor carries 2 A.

questions.stem: Conductance is the reciprocal of
questions.explanation: G = 1/R, measured in siemens (S); conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity.

questions.stem: A current of 0.8 A flows in a wire for 2 s. How many electrons pass a point in the wire? (e = 1.6 x 10^(-19) C)
questions.explanation: Q = It = 1.6 C; number of electrons = 1.6/(1.6 x 10^(-19)) = 1.0 x 10^19.

questions.stem: An electric iron of resistance 60 ohms is connected to a 240 V supply. Find its power rating.
A household uses a 1.5 kW pressing iron for 2 hours a day and a 500 W fridge for 6 hours a day. If electricity costs ₦70 per kWh, find the cost for 30 days.
questions.explanation: Daily energy = 1.5 x 2 + 0.5 x 6 = 6 kWh; monthly = 180 kWh; cost = 180 x 70 = ₦12,600.

questions.stem: A 2.4 kW water heater is used on a 240 V mains supply. Which is the most suitable fuse rating?
questions.explanation: The normal current is 2400/240 = 10 A; the fuse should be slightly above this, so 13 A.

questions.stem: A current of 3 A flows through a 20 ohm resistor for 1 minute. Find the heat produced.
Electrical power is transmitted over long distances at very high voltages in order to
options: reduce the current and so reduce I^2 R power loss in the cables
increase the current in the cables
increase the resistance of the cables
questions.explanation: For a given power P = VI, a higher V means a smaller I, and the heating loss I^2 R falls sharply.

questions.stem: In house wiring, the fuse and the switch should be connected in the
questions.explanation: This ensures that the appliance is disconnected from the high potential when the switch is off or the fuse blows.

questions.stem: The commercial unit of electrical energy is the
A bulb rated 100 W, 240 V is connected to a 120 V supply. Assuming its resistance is constant, find the power it now dissipates.
questions.explanation: R = 240^2/100 = 576 ohms; P = 120^2/576 = 25 W. Halving V quarters the power.

questions.stem: A current of 50 A flows through transmission cables of total resistance 4 ohms. Find the power lost as heat in the cables.
A 60 W bulb is switched on for 5 hours every day. How much energy does it use in 30 days?
questions.explanation: E = 0.06 kW x 5 h x 30 = 9 kWh.

questions.stem: Soft iron is used for the cores of electromagnets because it
questions.explanation: Soft iron has high permeability and low retentivity.

questions.stem: Steel is preferred to soft iron for making permanent magnets because steel
questions.explanation: Steel is harder to magnetise but keeps its magnetism once magnetised.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods will demagnetise a magnet?
options: Placing it in a solenoid carrying direct current
questions.explanation: Heating (or hammering, or slowly withdrawing it from an a.c. solenoid) disorders the domains.

questions.stem: The angle between the earth's magnetic meridian and the geographic meridian at a place is called the
options: angle of inclination of the field to the vertical
questions.explanation: Dip (inclination) is the angle the earth's field makes with the horizontal.

questions.stem: At a place where the declination is 8 degrees W, a compass needle points along N 35 degrees E (magnetic). What is the true (geographic) bearing of the direction?
questions.explanation: Magnetic north lies 8 degrees west of true north, so a magnetic bearing of N 35 degrees E is true N (35 - 8) = 27 degrees E.

questions.stem: A magnetic needle that is free to turn in a vertical plane is taken to a place on the magnetic equator. How does it come to rest?
options: Vertically, because the angle of dip there is 90 degrees
Horizontally, because the angle of dip there is 0 degrees
It keeps spinning and never settles
questions.explanation: At the magnetic equator the earth's field is horizontal, so a dip needle settles horizontally; at the magnetic poles it would hang vertically.

questions.stem: The magnetic field lines around a long straight wire carrying current are
options: straight lines parallel to the wire
straight lines radiating from the wire
concentric circles centred on the wire
questions.explanation: The direction of the circles is given by the right-hand grip rule.

questions.stem: A neutral point in a magnetic field is a point where
options: the resultant magnetic field is zero
questions.explanation: At a neutral point the field of the magnet exactly cancels the earth's horizontal field.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: A wire 20 cm long carrying 4 A lies at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. Find the force on the wire.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: A wire 20 cm long carrying 4 A makes an angle of 30 degrees with a uniform 0.5 T magnetic field. Find the force on it.
questions.explanation: F = BIL sin(theta) = 0.4 x sin 30 = 0.2 N.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: An electron moves at 2.0 x 10^6 m/s at right angles to a magnetic field of 0.3 T. Find the magnetic force on it. (e = 1.6 x 10^(-19) C)

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: The direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: In the left-hand rule the first finger is Field, the second finger is Current and the thumb is Motion (thrust).

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: Two long parallel wires carry currents in the same direction. The wires
questions.explanation: Parallel currents in the same direction attract; opposite directions repel.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: A galvanometer of resistance 50 ohms gives full-scale deflection with 10 mA. What shunt resistance converts it into an ammeter reading up to 5 A?
questions.explanation: The shunt carries 5 - 0.01 = 4.99 A at the same p.d. (0.01 x 50 = 0.5 V): R = 0.5/4.99 = 0.1 ohm, connected in parallel.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: A galvanometer of resistance 50 ohms gives full-scale deflection with 10 mA. What resistance in series converts it into a voltmeter reading up to 10 V?
questions.explanation: Total resistance needed = 10/0.01 = 1000 ohms; multiplier = 1000 - 50 = 950 ohms.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: In a d.c. motor, the split-ring commutator
options: converts a.c. to d.c. in the supply
reverses the current in the coil every half turn
questions.explanation: Reversing the current keeps the torque in the same direction so the coil keeps rotating.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: The sensitivity of a moving-coil galvanometer can be increased by
options: increasing the number of turns on the coil
reducing the strength of the magnet
reducing the area of the coil
questions.explanation: Deflection is proportional to BANI/k, so more turns (or a stronger field, larger area or weaker spring) increase sensitivity.

questions.stem: The magnetic flux through each turn of a 200-turn coil falls from 0.5 Wb to 0.1 Wb in 0.2 s. Find the average induced e.m.f.
questions.explanation: e = N(change in flux)/t = 200 x 0.4/0.2 = 400 V.

questions.stem: A transformer has 1200 turns in its primary and 60 turns in its secondary. If the primary voltage is 240 V, find the secondary voltage.
questions.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, so Vs = 240 x 60/1200 = 12 V.

questions.stem: A transformer that is 80% efficient steps 240 V down to 12 V. If the secondary current is 4 A, find the primary current.
questions.explanation: Output power = 12 x 4 = 48 W; input = 48/0.8 = 60 W; Ip = 60/240 = 0.25 A.

questions.stem: Lenz's law is a consequence of the principle of conservation of
questions.explanation: The induced current opposes the change producing it, so work must be done to generate electrical energy.

questions.stem: The e.m.f. induced in a coil rotating in a magnetic field can be increased by
options: reducing the area of the coil
questions.explanation: Peak e.m.f. = NAB(omega), so it rises with speed, turns, area and field strength.

questions.stem: A straight conductor 0.5 m long moves at 3 m/s at right angles to a magnetic field of 0.4 T. Find the e.m.f. induced across its ends.
An a.c. generator differs from a d.c. generator in that the a.c. generator uses
questions.explanation: Slip rings keep each end of the coil connected to the same brush, so the output alternates.

questions.stem: A transformer will NOT work on a steady d.c. supply because
options: a steady current produces no changing magnetic flux
d.c. flows only in the secondary
questions.explanation: Induction requires a changing flux linking the secondary coil.

questions.stem: The induction coil is used to produce
options: high voltages from a low-voltage d.c. source
questions.explanation: A make-and-break interrupts the primary current, inducing large e.m.f.s in the many-turn secondary (as in car ignition systems).

questions.stem: Find the energy stored in an inductor of 0.4 H carrying a current of 3 A.
The SI unit of inductance is the
questions.explanation: 1 henry is the inductance in which a current changing at 1 A/s induces an e.m.f. of 1 V.

questions.stem: The current in a coil of self-inductance 0.2 H falls from 5 A to zero in 0.01 s. Find the average e.m.f. induced.
questions.explanation: e = L(change in current)/t = 0.2 x 5/0.01 = 100 V.

questions.stem: Self-inductance in a coil opposes
options: the steady current in the coil
the magnetic field of the earth
changes in the current flowing through it
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law the back e.m.f. opposes any change in current.

questions.stem: Inductors (chokes) are used in fluorescent lamp circuits to
options: produce a high e.m.f. to start the lamp and limit the current
questions.explanation: Breaking the current in the choke induces a large e.m.f. that strikes the discharge.

questions.stem: Why is the soft-iron core of a transformer built from thin insulated sheets instead of a solid block?
options: To make the core a permanent magnet
To increase the resistance of the copper windings
To reduce energy lost through eddy currents
questions.explanation: Insulated laminations break up the paths of induced (eddy) currents in the core, reducing heating losses.

questions.stem: Which of the following makes use of eddy currents?
options: Electric bell with a permanent magnet only
questions.explanation: Changing magnetic fields induce eddy currents in the metal pan, heating it.

questions.stem: A copper plate swinging between the poles of a strong magnet quickly comes to rest because
options: eddy currents induced in the plate oppose its motion
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law the eddy currents produce forces that damp the motion (electromagnetic damping).

questions.stem: The moving coil of a galvanometer is wound on an aluminium frame so that
options: the coil is insulated from the magnet
eddy currents in the frame damp its oscillations
questions.explanation: Damping lets the pointer settle quickly at its final reading.

questions.stem: The r.m.s. voltage of the mains is 240 V. Find its peak value.
questions.explanation: V(peak) = sqrt(2) x V(rms) = 1.414 x 240 = 339 V.

questions.stem: An alternating current has a peak value of 5 A. Find its r.m.s. value.
questions.explanation: I(rms) = I(peak)/sqrt(2) = 3.54 A.

questions.stem: Find the inductive reactance of a 0.2 H inductor in a 50 Hz a.c. circuit.
questions.explanation: X(L) = 2 pi f L = 2 pi x 50 x 0.2 = 20 pi, about 62.8 ohms.

questions.stem: Find the capacitive reactance of a 100 microfarad capacitor in a 50 Hz circuit.
A series circuit contains a resistance of 30 ohms, an inductive reactance of 70 ohms and a capacitive reactance of 30 ohms. Find the impedance.
For a series circuit with R = 30 ohms, X(L) = 70 ohms and X(C) = 30 ohms, find the power factor.
questions.explanation: Power factor = cos(phi) = R/Z = 30/50 = 0.6.

questions.stem: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with an inductor of 0.1 H and a capacitor of 10 microfarads.
In a purely capacitive a.c. circuit, the current
options: is in phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: In a pure inductor the current lags by 90 degrees; in a pure resistor current and voltage are in phase.

questions.stem: In a series R-L-C circuit at resonance
options: the impedance equals the resistance and the current is maximum
questions.explanation: X(L) = X(C), so they cancel and Z = R.

questions.stem: An a.c. circuit draws an r.m.s. current of 5 A from a 240 V r.m.s. supply with a power factor of 0.8. Find the average power consumed.
questions.explanation: P = V(rms) I(rms) cos(phi) = 240 x 5 x 0.8 = 960 W.

questions.stem: A current of 2 A is passed through copper sulphate solution for 30 minutes. Find the mass of copper deposited. (electrochemical equivalent of copper = 3.3 x 10^(-7) kg/C)
How long will it take a current of 1.0 A to deposit 0.66 g of copper on a cathode? (z for copper = 3.3 x 10^(-7) kg/C)
Which of the following is a non-electrolyte?
questions.explanation: Sugar does not ionise in water, so the solution does not conduct.

questions.stem: In electroplating a spoon with silver, the spoon is made the
questions.explanation: Positive silver ions are attracted to the negative electrode (cathode) and deposit there.

questions.stem: Faraday's first law of electrolysis states that the mass of a substance liberated is proportional to the
questions.explanation: m = zQ = zIt.

questions.stem: In the electrolysis of acidulated water, the volume of hydrogen produced compared with oxygen is
questions.explanation: Water (H2O) contains two hydrogen atoms for each oxygen atom, giving H2 and O2 in the ratio 2 : 1 by volume.

questions.stem: The same current is passed through copper and silver voltameters in series for the same time. If 0.635 g of copper (Cu2+, relative atomic mass 63.5) is deposited, what mass of silver (Ag+, relative atomic mass 108) is deposited?
questions.explanation: Charge passed = 0.635/63.5 x 2 moles of electrons = 0.02 mol; silver deposited = 0.02 x 108 = 2.16 g (Faraday's second law).

questions.stem: Gases at ordinary pressure are poor conductors of electricity because
options: they contain very few free ions or electrons
they are always at high temperature
questions.explanation: Conduction requires charge carriers; ionisation (by high voltage, heat or radiation) is needed to make a gas conduct.

questions.stem: Cathode rays are streams of
questions.explanation: They are deflected by electric and magnetic fields in the way expected for negative particles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an application of electrical discharge through gases?
questions.explanation: Discharge excites mercury vapour in the tube, which emits UV that makes the coating fluoresce.

questions.stem: When the pressure in a discharge tube is reduced to a very low value at high voltage, the tube
options: becomes dark and the glass at the far end glows
questions.explanation: At very low pressure the electrons travel freely (cathode rays) and strike the glass, making it fluoresce.

questions.stem: Neon advertising signs glow because
options: electric discharge excites the gas atoms, which emit light
the tube is heated to white heat
questions.explanation: Excited atoms emit light of colours characteristic of the gas.

questions.stem: Find the energy of a photon of wavelength 6.6 x 10^(-7) m. (h = 6.6 x 10^(-34) J s, c = 3.0 x 10^8 m/s)
Light of frequency 8.0 x 10^14 Hz falls on a metal of work function 2.0 eV. Find the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons. (h = 6.6 x 10^(-34) J s, 1 eV = 1.6 x 10^(-19) J)
Find the threshold frequency for a metal whose work function is 2.0 eV. (h = 6.6 x 10^(-34) J s, 1 eV = 1.6 x 10^(-19) J)
An electron in a hydrogen atom falls from the energy level -3.4 eV to the ground state at -13.6 eV. What is the energy of the photon emitted?
questions.explanation: Photon energy = difference between the levels = -3.4 - (-13.6) = 10.2 eV.

questions.stem: A radioactive source has a half-life of 6 hours. If 64 g is present initially, how much remains undecayed after 24 hours?
questions.explanation: 24 hours is 4 half-lives: 64 x (1/2)^4 = 4 g.

questions.stem: The activity of a radioactive sample falls from 800 counts per minute to 100 counts per minute in 30 days. Find its half-life.
questions.explanation: 800 to 100 is a fall by a factor of 8 = 2^3, i.e. 3 half-lives in 30 days, so T = 10 days.

questions.stem: When a nucleus emits an alpha particle, its mass number and atomic number respectively
options: stay the same and decrease by 1
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus with mass number 4 and atomic number 2.

questions.stem: When a nucleus emits a beta particle, its
options: atomic number increases by 1 and its mass number is unchanged
questions.explanation: A neutron changes into a proton and an electron; the electron is emitted.

questions.stem: Uranium-238 (atomic number 92) decays to lead-206 (atomic number 82) by a series of alpha and beta emissions. How many alpha and beta particles are emitted?
questions.explanation: Mass falls by 32, so 8 alpha particles; these lower Z by 16 to 76, so 6 beta emissions raise it back to 82.

questions.stem: Which of the following radiations is the most penetrating?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are uncharged high-energy photons and need thick lead or concrete to stop them.

questions.stem: Alpha particles are deflected only slightly in a magnetic field compared with beta particles because alpha particles
questions.explanation: Although they carry twice the charge, alpha particles are about 7000 times more massive than electrons.

questions.stem: In the Rutherford scattering experiment, the fact that a few alpha particles bounced back showed that
options: the positive charge and most of the mass of an atom are concentrated in a tiny nucleus
questions.explanation: Large-angle scattering needs a concentrated, massive positive centre.

questions.stem: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, an electron emits radiation only when it
options: jumps from a higher to a lower energy level
questions.explanation: Electrons in allowed orbits do not radiate; a photon of energy hf = E2 - E1 is emitted in a transition.

questions.stem: Photoelectrons are emitted with a maximum kinetic energy of 2.08 x 10^(-19) J. Find the stopping potential. (e = 1.6 x 10^(-19) C)
X-rays are produced when
options: light falls on a metal surface
fast-moving electrons are suddenly stopped by a metal target
questions.explanation: The kinetic energy of the decelerated electrons is partly converted to X-ray photons.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides evidence of the particle (photon) nature of light?
questions.explanation: Emission depends on frequency, not intensity, which can only be explained using photons; the other three are wave effects.

questions.stem: Find the de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving at 2.0 x 10^6 m/s. (h = 6.6 x 10^(-34) J s, mass of electron = 9.1 x 10^(-31) kg)
Thermionic emission is the emission of electrons from
questions.explanation: Heating gives some electrons enough energy to escape; this is used in cathode-ray tubes and X-ray tubes.

questions.stem: In nuclear fusion
options: a heavy nucleus splits into lighter nuclei
light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus with release of energy
neutrons are absorbed without energy change
questions.explanation: Fusion of hydrogen isotopes powers the sun; fission is the splitting of heavy nuclei.

questions.stem: What fraction of a radioactive sample has decayed after three half-lives?
questions.explanation: The fraction remaining is (1/2)^3 = 1/8, so 7/8 has decayed.

questions.stem: An n-type semiconductor is formed by doping pure silicon with
options: a pentavalent element such as phosphorus
a trivalent element such as boron
questions.explanation: Each pentavalent atom donates a free electron, so electrons are the majority carriers.

questions.stem: The majority charge carriers in a p-type semiconductor are
questions.explanation: Trivalent impurities create holes that act as positive carriers.

questions.stem: A p-n junction diode is mainly used for
questions.explanation: The diode conducts in only one direction, converting a.c. into (pulsating) d.c.

questions.stem: A p-n junction is forward biased when
options: the n-side is connected to the positive terminal
the p-side is connected to the positive terminal of the battery
questions.explanation: Forward bias narrows the depletion layer and allows current to flow.

questions.stem: Semiconductors differ from metals in that the resistance of a pure semiconductor
questions.explanation: Heating frees more electron-hole pairs in a semiconductor, while in metals it increases lattice vibrations.

questions.stem: In terms of energy bands, an insulator has
options: a large forbidden gap between the valence and conduction bands
questions.explanation: Electrons cannot easily gain enough energy to cross a wide band gap.

questions.stem: A transistor is mainly used as
questions.explanation: A small base current controls a much larger collector current.

questions.stem: In a transistor circuit, a base current of 50 microamperes produces a collector current of 4 mA. Find the current gain.
A full-wave rectifier differs from a half-wave rectifier in that it
options: uses both halves of each a.c. cycle
questions.explanation: A bridge of four diodes (or two with a centre-tapped transformer) conducts in both half-cycles.

questions.stem: A driver travelling at 30 m/s sees an obstruction. Her reaction time is 0.5 s, after which the car decelerates uniformly at 5 m/s^2. Find the total stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Thinking distance = 30 x 0.5 = 15 m; braking distance = 30^2/(2 x 5) = 90 m; total = 105 m.

questions.stem: A ball is kicked horizontally at 20 m/s from the top of a cliff 45 m high. How far from the foot of the cliff does it land? (g = 10 m/s^2; ignore air resistance)
questions.explanation: Time to fall = sqrt(2 x 45/10) = 3 s; horizontal distance = 20 x 3 = 60 m.

questions.stem: A stone is dropped from rest. How far does it fall during the third second of its motion? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: Distance in 3 s = 45 m; in 2 s = 20 m; so in the third second it falls 25 m.

questions.stem: Masses of 3 kg and 2 kg hang on either side of a light frictionless pulley by a light inextensible string. Find the tension in the string. (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: a = (3 - 2)g/(3 + 2) = 2 m/s^2; for the 2 kg mass T - 20 = 2 x 2, so T = 24 N.

questions.stem: A block slides down a smooth plane inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal. Starting from rest, what is its speed after 2 s? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: The acceleration along a smooth incline is g sin 30 = 5 m/s^2, so v = 5 x 2 = 10 m/s.

questions.stem: A car moving at 15 m/s accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s^2 over a distance of 100 m. Find its final speed.
Find the speed of a satellite orbiting just above the Earth's surface. (g = 10 m/s^2, radius of the Earth = 6.4 x 10^6 m)
questions.explanation: For a close orbit mg = mv^2/R, so v = sqrt(gR) = sqrt(6.4 x 10^7) = 8000 m/s = 8.0 km/s.

questions.stem: A 100 N weight is supported by two strings attached to a ceiling, making angles of 30 degrees and 60 degrees with the horizontal. Find the tension in the string inclined at 60 degrees.
questions.explanation: Horizontally T1 cos 30 = T2 cos 60; vertically T1 sin 30 + T2 sin 60 = 100. These give T1 = 50 N and T2 = 50 sqrt(3) N (about 86.6 N); the steeper string carries more of the load.

questions.stem: A pump that is 80% efficient raises 500 kg of water through a height of 20 m in 50 s. Find the power input to the pump. (g = 10 m/s^2)
A 3 kg trolley moving at 4 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg trolley and they stick together. How much kinetic energy is lost?
questions.explanation: The common velocity is 3 m/s. KE before = 24 J and after = 0.5 x 4 x 9 = 18 J, so 6 J is lost. Momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not.

questions.stem: A box slides down a plane inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal. If the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2, find its acceleration. (g = 10 m/s^2)
A pulley system of velocity ratio 5 needs an effort of 250 N to raise a load of 1000 N through 2 m. How much work is wasted?
questions.explanation: The effort moves 5 x 2 = 10 m: work input = 2500 J; work output = 1000 x 2 = 2000 J; wasted = 500 J.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A wire is stretched within its elastic limit so that the stress is 2.0 x 10^8 N/m^2 and the strain is 1.0 x 10^(-3). Find the energy stored per unit volume.
questions.explanation: Energy per unit volume = (1/2) x stress x strain = 0.5 x 2.0 x 10^8 x 1.0 x 10^(-3) = 1.0 x 10^5 J/m^3.

questions.stem: In a U-tube, a column of water 34 cm high balances a column of mercury. If the relative density of mercury is 13.6, find the height of the mercury column.
questions.explanation: Equal pressures: 34 x 1 = h x 13.6, so h = 2.5 cm.

questions.stem: A block floats in water with three-quarters of its volume submerged, and in a certain liquid with two-thirds of its volume submerged. Find the density of the liquid. (density of water = 1000 kg/m^3)
questions.explanation: The block's density is 3/4 x 1000 = 750 kg/m^3; in the liquid 750 = (2/3) rho, so rho = 1125 kg/m^3.

questions.stem: An air bubble rises from the bed of a lake 30 m deep to the surface. If atmospheric pressure is equivalent to 10 m of water and the temperature is constant, by what factor does the volume of the bubble increase?
questions.explanation: Pressure at the bed = 30 + 10 = 40 m of water; at the surface = 10 m of water; by Boyle's law the volume increases by 40/10 = 4 times.

questions.stem: Steam at 100 degrees C is passed into 0.5 kg of water at 20 degrees C until the temperature reaches 60 degrees C. Find the mass of steam condensed. (c of water = 4200 J/(kg K), latent heat of vaporisation = 2.26 x 10^6 J/kg; ignore heat losses)
questions.explanation: Heat given by steam = m(2.26 x 10^6 + 4200 x 40); heat gained by water = 0.5 x 4200 x 40 = 84,000 J. So m = 84,000/2,428,000 = 0.0346 kg, about 34.6 g.

questions.stem: Calculate the heat needed to convert 50 g of ice at -10 degrees C into water at 20 degrees C. (c of ice = 2100 J/(kg K), latent heat of fusion = 336 000 J/kg, c of water = 4200 J/(kg K))
questions.explanation: Warming ice: 0.05 x 2100 x 10 = 1050 J; melting: 0.05 x 336,000 = 16,800 J; warming water: 0.05 x 4200 x 20 = 4200 J; total = 22,050 J.

questions.stem: The apparent cubic expansivity of a liquid in a glass vessel is 1.5 x 10^(-4) per K. If the linear expansivity of glass is 9 x 10^(-6) per K, find the real cubic expansivity of the liquid.
questions.explanation: Real = apparent + cubic expansivity of glass = 1.5 x 10^(-4) + 3(9 x 10^(-6)) = 1.77 x 10^(-4) per K.

questions.stem: A string 1.2 m long, fixed at both ends, vibrates in three loops at a frequency of 150 Hz. Find the speed of waves on the string.
questions.explanation: Three loops occupy 1.5 wavelengths, so the wavelength = 2 x 1.2/3 = 0.8 m; v = 150 x 0.8 = 120 m/s.

questions.stem: An open pipe 85 cm long is sounded. Find the frequency of its second overtone. (speed of sound = 340 m/s)
questions.explanation: For an open pipe the harmonics are n(v/2L), with v/2L = 200 Hz. The second overtone is the third harmonic: 3 x 200 = 600 Hz.

questions.stem: In a resonance-tube experiment with a 512 Hz tuning fork, the first two resonance lengths are 16.0 cm and 50.0 cm. Find the speed of sound in air.
questions.explanation: The difference between successive resonance lengths is half a wavelength: wavelength = 2(0.50 - 0.16) = 0.68 m, so v = 512 x 0.68 = 348.2 m/s, about 348 m/s.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm forms an upright image three times the size of the object. How far is the object from the mirror?
questions.explanation: An upright magnified image is virtual, so v = -3u. Then 1/u - 1/(3u) = 1/15 gives 2/(3u) = 1/15 and u = 10 cm.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A converging lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a diverging lens of focal length 30 cm. Find the focal length of the combination.
questions.explanation: 1/F = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60, so F = +60 cm: the combination is converging.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: Find the critical angle for light passing from glass (refractive index 1.5) into water (refractive index 4/3).
questions.explanation: sin C = n(water)/n(glass) = (4/3)/1.5 = 8/9, so C = 62.7 degrees.

questions.stem: Point charges of +4 microcoulombs and +9 microcoulombs are 50 cm apart. How far from the +4 microcoulomb charge, on the line joining them, is the electric field zero?
questions.explanation: At the null point 4/x^2 = 9/(0.5 - x)^2, so 2/x = 3/(0.5 - x), giving x = 0.2 m. The point is nearer the smaller charge.

questions.stem: A 4 microfarad capacitor charged to 100 V is connected across an uncharged 6 microfarad capacitor. Find the common potential difference.
questions.explanation: Charge is conserved: Q = 4 x 10^(-6) x 100 = 4 x 10^(-4) C, shared by 10 microfarads, so V = 40 V.

questions.stem: A battery of e.m.f. 12 V and internal resistance 2 ohms supplies an external resistor R. Find the maximum power that can be delivered to R.
questions.explanation: Maximum power transfer occurs when R = r = 2 ohms: I = 12/4 = 3 A and P = 3^2 x 2 = 18 W.

questions.stem: On a potentiometer, a cell balances at 80 cm on open circuit and at 60 cm when a 6 ohm resistor is connected across it. Find the internal resistance of the cell.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: Two long parallel wires 10 cm apart in air carry currents of 10 A and 5 A. Find the force per metre between them. (permeability of free space = 4 pi x 10^(-7) H/m)
A coil of 100 turns, each of area 0.02 m^2, rotates at 100 rad/s in a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. Find the peak e.m.f. induced.
A 40 ohm resistor and a capacitor of reactance 30 ohms are in series across a 100 V r.m.s. a.c. supply. Find the average power dissipated.
questions.explanation: Z = sqrt(40^2 + 30^2) = 50 ohms, I = 100/50 = 2 A, and only the resistor dissipates power: P = I^2 R = 4 x 40 = 160 W.

questions.stem: A current of 0.5 A flows through silver nitrate solution for 1 hour. Find the mass of silver deposited. (Ag+, relative atomic mass 108; Faraday constant = 96 500 C/mol)
An X-ray tube operates at 50 kV. Find the maximum frequency of the X-rays produced. (e = 1.6 x 10^(-19) C, h = 6.6 x 10^(-34) J s)
questions.explanation: All the electron's energy eV becomes one photon: f = eV/h = (1.6 x 10^(-19) x 5 x 10^4)/(6.6 x 10^(-34)) = 1.2 x 10^19 Hz.

questions.stem: After 2 hours, only one-sixteenth of a radioactive sample remains undecayed. Find its half-life.
questions.explanation: 1/16 = (1/2)^4, so 4 half-lives take 120 minutes and each is 30 minutes.
